text: For about half a year I had panic attacks in crowded places and whenever there was a lot of wind or dust. I had a strange feeling of unreality for weeks, like the world had ended and this was some kind of afterlife. I stopped going to festivals completely. I also became quite obsessed with news about nuclear war and climate disasters, which I'd never cared much about before.

Danach hatte ich lange Zeit Angst, dass mein Atem aufhört, vor allem beim Einschlafen. Ich habe ständig auf meinen Herzschlag geachtet. Ich hatte mehrere Panikattacken und war noch zweimal in der Notaufnahme.

Since that experience, which was four years ago, I've had depersonalisation almost every day. I feel like I'm not fully in my body, like I'm watching myself from a few inches behind my own head. When I talk, it sounds like someone else's voice. The world looks two-dimensional, like a picture. In the first year I also had visual snow and very strong afterimages, which have gotten a bit better.

I developed depression in the first year. I couldn't feel joy or love properly, everything was muted. I felt like I'd lost my soul, which is what it felt like during the trip, that it left and never fully came back. I had suicidal thoughts for months because I couldn't imagine living like this forever. I had to drop out of my apprenticeship.

I also have a lot of anxiety about the DP itself, I check constantly whether I feel 'real'. I've had several panic attacks where I felt like I was about to completely lose myself again. I avoid anything that might alter my consciousness, even alcohol and caffeine.

It's better than it was in the first year, but I don't think I've ever been fully myself since.

The memories of the assault kept coming back for months, especially during intimacy. I avoided sex for almost a year. I felt guilty towards my partner. But I also think the trip forced me to face something I had buried for a long time, and I'm glad in a way it came out.

In the months after, I had panic attacks that always involved breathing. I'd suddenly feel like I couldn't get air and I'd gasp. It would happen in the shower, when I put my face in water, when I had a cold and my nose was blocked, and sometimes for no reason at all, lying in bed. I avoided swimming completely, which I used to love. I had nightmares about water. I also had some days of feeling very far away from myself.

At the same time, I learned something big about my life. Discovering the near-drowning explained a lot about my lifelong anxiety, my fear of losing control, my need to always know where the exits are. In a strange way, it was a relief to finally have a reason.
Jumpy around alarms and loud sudden noises, a bit anxious in general for a few months.

The weeks after that night were the start of the worst depression I've had. I'm not sure if it was the drugs, or the feeling of being abandoned, or both. I couldn't get out of bed, I didn't want to see anyone, I cried a lot for no clear reason. I couldn't feel anything good, food had no taste, music sounded like noise. I had a strong feeling that nobody actually cares about me and that my friends just tolerated me. I stopped answering their messages, which of course made it worse.

Around two months later I started having suicidal thoughts every day. I didn't act on them but I thought about it a lot and looked things up. I had a lot of anxiety too, mostly in social situations, I was convinced that people were laughing at me behind my back.

It took over a year for the depression to lift. I lost my job during that time because I couldn't work. I also lost most of my friends from that group. I've made new friends since, but I still find it hard to trust people.

Nach der Zeremonie hatte ich viele Monate lang Albträume mit dunklen Gestalten und konnte nicht im Dunkeln schlafen. Ich war misstrauisch gegenüber allen, die in spirituellen Kreisen eine Leitungsrolle haben. Ich hatte auch Angst, meine Wohnung zu verlassen, wenn es dunkel war. Rückblickend hat mir die Erfahrung aber gezeigt, wie wichtig es ist, auf mein Bauchgefühl zu hören, das mich schon vorher gewarnt hatte.
Guilt and a bit of anxiety, nothing big. It passed.

Ich hatte danach lange Zeit starke soziale Ängste, vor allem bei Feiern und wenn ich vor Leuten sprechen musste. Ich habe mich bei meinem Freund entschuldigt, aber das Verhältnis ist nicht mehr dasselbe.
